chapter: Orchestra people and Xavier chamber concerts
title: Ettore Fontana, personnel manager and source of Civic show work
summary: Fontana, a Milan-born trombonist turned Sanger Theatre and symphony personnel manager, hired Mazzari for Broadway shows and ice shows at good pay; his work ended after Fontana died.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Who's this fellow, Fontana, you asked me?

Oh, Fontana is an old Italian immigrant from Milan, Italy, who came here and came here with an opera. I think they got stranded here. So he'd been here ever since. He was a trombone player and he wound up as a orchestra manager at Sanger, the old Sanger Theatre, you know? And then he became a personnel manager with the symphony here. Ettore Fontana. He was a real nice fellow. He was, in fact, he booked all the Broadway musicals at the Civic and that's how I got to play them all, you know? Because he hired me every time.
And that made him especially nice, I guess.

Oh, yes. That was good money, you know? On the pit, you know, play nine, ten shows, you get a hundred and fifty, a hundred and sixty, a hundred and seventy dollars. I used to do the ice shows too when they came to town here. Same thing, good money. But since he died, somebody else took charge of all these big job deals and all of a sudden I was out. It's politics, you see? You're in one day, out the other.

Oh, he was a very unassuming person. He didn't try to put on an act like some people do. He was very pleasant and affable. And he tried to, of course, being a personnel manager is quite a job, you know? You got to please the conductor and you got to please the musicians too. You're the guy in the middle. Boy, that's a hell of a job to be in. Of course, the first thing you know is if something happens, oh, they'll say he's kissing the conductor's ass, you know? Things like that. But I think Fontana did a pretty good job of it. And having known several personnel managers in various orchestras, I think Mr. Fontana was by far the best. He was nice to talk to. We always talked in Italian together. Of course, being from Milan, he talked, he knew his Milanese dialect, but he talked pure Italian too when he wanted to. So I enjoyed talking to him.
